original: For many years, intelligence was measured mainly by IQ, or Intelligence Quotient. People believed that academic knowledge and logical reasoning were the most reliable predictors of success. correction: IQ tests assess some cognitive abilities, but they do not describe every skill people use in daily life. A person may solve complex problems yet struggle to listen, handle frustration, or work with others. Emotional intelligence provides a way to discuss how people understand emotions and respond to them.
reason: Remove the unsupported historical/predictive comparison between IQ and emotional intelligence.

original: Psychologist Daniel Goleman popularized the concept of emotional intelligence by identifying five essential components: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skills. Self-awareness allows people to recognize their emotional state and understand how their feelings influence their behavior. Self-regulation enables them to control emotional reactions instead of acting impulsively. Motivation encourages people to pursue long-term goals despite setbacks. Empathy involves understanding the feelings and perspectives of others, while social skills help individuals communicate effectively and build meaningful relationships.
correction: In the model popularized by psychologist Daniel Goleman, emotional intelligence includes five components: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skills. Self-awareness allows people to recognize their emotional state and understand how their feelings influence their behavior. Self-regulation enables them to control emotional reactions instead of acting impulsively. Motivation encourages people to pursue long-term goals despite setbacks. Empathy involves understanding the feelings and perspectives of others, while social skills help individuals communicate effectively and build meaningful relationships.
reason: Attribute the five-part model without presenting it as the only universally established definition.
